# SegmentedControl

Use SegmentedControl when users choose one option from a short, visible set. Prefer Radio for longer lists and Tabs when the selected item changes visible content regions.

- **Import:** `import { SegmentedControl } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Selection
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/selection-segmentedcontrol--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl, ThemeProvider } from "@kozmos-ds/react";

const items = [
  { value: "overview", label: "Overview" },
  { value: "details", label: "Details" },
  { value: "activity", label: "Activity" },
];

export function SegmentedControlExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <SegmentedControl defaultValue="overview" items={items} />
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## SegmentedControl

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `SegmentedControlProps`, which extends `Omit<React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof ToggleGroupPrimitive.Root>, "defaultValue" | "onValueChange" | "type" | "value">, VariantProps<typeof segmentedControlVariants>`.

- `defaultValue`: `string`, optional.
- `error`: `boolean | string`, optional.
- `fullWidth`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.
- `items`: `SegmentedControlItem[]`, **required**.
- `label`: `string`, optional.
- `onValueChange`: `(value: string | undefined) => void`, optional.

  Called with the pressed value, or `undefined` when the reviewer presses the
  segment that already holds the pill and takes their choice back.

  The `undefined` is the point. Radix reports a deselect as `""`, which is a
  value no `items` entry can ever have, and every consumer had to know that
  and guard it. One of them cast it to a union that did not include it, and
  the cast laundered an impossible value past TypeScript — it survived only
  because `""` is falsy and every reader happened to treat it as "nothing
  chosen". Normalising to `undefined` makes the empty case something the type
  system can see, so the compiler asks the question instead of the reviewer
  discovering it.

  A consumer that wants "exactly one, always" should control `value` and
  ignore the `undefined` rather than expect the component to refuse it.

- `size`: `"sm" | "default" | "lg"`, optional, default `"default"`.
- `value`: `string`, optional.

  The chosen segment, for a product that holds the choice itself. Passed at
  all, `value` holds it: `undefined` is nothing chosen, the value
  `onValueChange` hands over when the choice is taken back, so a control
  that starts empty passes `value={undefined}` too. Leave it out, and give
  `defaultValue`, for a control that keeps its own choice; an `undefined`
  value beside a `defaultValue` leaves the choice to the control as well.

- `wrapperClassName`: `string`, optional.
- `dir`: `RovingFocusGroupProps['dir']`, optional.
- `asChild`: `boolean`, optional.
- `disabled`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.

  Whether the group is disabled from user interaction.

- `loop`: `RovingFocusGroupProps['loop']`, optional.
- `orientation`: `RovingFocusGroupProps['orientation']`, optional.
- `rovingFocus`: `boolean`, optional, default `true`.

  Whether the group should maintain roving focus of its buttons.

- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## Types these props take

### SegmentedControlItem

From `@kozmos-ds/react`.

```ts
type SegmentedControlItem = {
  disabled?: boolean;
  label: React.ReactNode;
  value: string;
};
```
